rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly, so this candidate escalates obfuscation across all seven passes. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain because the target is the recursive Ackermann kernel plus a main driver whose control flow is the primary reverse-engineering anchor; flattening the small function bodies destroys the recognizable recursive/branch structure cheaply given only 333 text bytes of baseline. SPLIT is weighted with maximal DiversityGain and minimal costs since it composes synergistically with FLA and BCF by creating more blocks to flatten and disguise, at near-zero runtime penalty. SUB and IBR are strongly favored (low costs, high gains) to scramble arithmetic and branch targets inside the tiny hot functions where static pattern matching is the main attack. BCF keeps a moderate RuntimeCost weight so bogus predicates are applied where features favor them but throttled in the deeply recursive Ack path, bounding runtime blowup on a recursive workload. ICALL and IGV round out coverage with indirect calls/globals to break call-graph and data-reference analysis; their CorrectnessRisk stays low-moderate since round 0 showed no ICE or miscompile. Overall costs remain well under the gains so the selector applies passes liberally while runtime/size overhead stays acceptable for this micro-kernel benchmark.
